## Web research: fs.watch on network drives

Question: "What do the Node.js docs at https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html say about using fs.watch on network drives?"
Pages: 1 read, 0 not fetched

### Facts
1. The docs say `fs.watch` behaves differently across platforms and does not work in some situations. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "The `fs.watch` API is not 100% consistent across platforms, and is unavailable in some situations."
2. The docs say that when the underlying OS feature is missing, `fs.watch()` will not work and may throw an exception. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "If the underlying functionality is not available for some reason, then `fs.watch()` will not be able to function and may throw an exception."
3. The docs name network file systems as a case where watching can be unreliable or impossible. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "watching files or directories can be unreliable, and in some cases impossible, on network file systems (NFS, SMB, etc)"
4. The same sentence adds host file systems mounted through virtualization software. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "...or host file systems when using virtualization software such as Vagrant or Docker."
5. The docs give `fs.watchFile()` (stat polling) as a fallback, but say it is slower and less reliable. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "It is still possible to use `fs.watchFile()`, which uses stat polling, but this method is slower and less reliable."
6. The docs say `fs.watch()` is more efficient than `fs.watchFile`. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Using fs.watch() is more efficient than `fs.watchFile` and `fs.unwatchFile`."
7. The page I read is the Node.js v26.13.1 documentation. Source: https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html "Node.js v26.13.1 Documentation"

### Inferences
- If a spec needs to watch a path on an NFS or SMB share, it shouldn't count on `fs.watch` alone. It needs to handle the case where `fs.watch` throws or misses changes (from facts 2, 3).
- The docs' only fallback for those cases is `fs.watchFile()` polling, which trades speed and reliability for wider support (from facts 5, 6).
- The docs don't promise that `fs.watch` works on any network file system. They only describe it as "unreliable, and in some cases impossible" there (from facts 1, 3).
